sections.h2: Where is the Davidson County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is in the Public Square Garage at 300 Deaderick Street, Nashville, TN 37201, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The mailing address is P.O. Box 196398, Nashville, TN 37219-6398. Anyone sending a deed by a courier other than the U.S. Postal Service has to use the street address instead of the box, and the phone line is 615-862-6790.

This is the office that keeps the county's warranty deeds, deeds of trust, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats. If you are selling a house in Nashville or elsewhere in Davidson County, the deed your buyer signs ends up here, and so does the paper that clears your old mortgage.

Davidson County is unusual in Tennessee because the city and the county have shared one government since 1963, called Metro Nashville. The register's office is a Metro department, so its web pages sit on nashville.gov next to the other Metro offices.

sections.h2: What does a seller get from the Davidson County register's app and online tools?
sections.html:
The register offers a free mobile app, listed in the Apple and Google stores as Nashville - Davidson Co. ROD, that puts several office services on a phone. It includes a fee calculator, buttons to call or email the staff, and the Property Alert sign-up.

Property Alert is worth a minute of a seller's time. It emails you if any document is filed under your name, which gives an early warning if someone tries to record a forged deed against your house. Many sellers only think about fraud after a closing goes wrong, and the sign-up is free.

  • Fee calculator for recording charges, on the office website and in the app
  • Property Alert email notices for filings under your name
  • Thank a Veteran program, which gives veterans a list of businesses offering discounts; veterans record their DD214 papers with the office in person
  • Online searching of recorded documents by subscription

The office's own FAQ says the staff will not draw up a deed, because a deed is a legal document and an attorney should prepare it. It also will not run a title search to tell you about liens, though the indexes are on public computers for anyone to use.

sections.h2: What does it cost to get copies of a Davidson County deed?
sections.html:
Copies of a recorded deed cost $0.50 a page uncertified and $1 a page certified. The same rates apply in person and by mail, but mailed requests carry a $2 minimum.

Copy charges at the Davidson County Register of Deeds
ItemChargeHow to get it
Uncertified copy$0.50 per pageIn person or by mail
Certified copy$1 per pageIn person or by mail
Mailed request$2 minimumWritten request with a stamped return envelope and payment
Subdivision plat by mail$5Written request

Source: Davidson County Register of Deeds, copies of deeds and documents. In person the office takes cash, checks, credit cards and money orders. A faxed copy is $1 a page, but only for customers who have opened an escrow account with the office first.

When you write for a copy, give the property address. If you want something other than a property deed, send as many details as you can so staff can find it in the indexes.

sections.h2: What does a deed need before the Davidson County register will record it?
sections.html:
The register decides whether a document is acceptable for recording, and the staff do not rule on whether the deed is legally sound. Under the training materials from the University of Tennessee's county advisory service, the deed has to meet the checklist below.

  • Be readable and carry a notarized acknowledgment, because Davidson's own FAQ says every signature must be notarized
  • Name the owner and the taxpayer, with addresses (T.C.A. 66-24-114)
  • Refer back to the earlier recorded deed (66-24-110)
  • Show who prepared it (66-24-115)
  • Give the parcel identification number (66-24-122)
  • Come with fees and any transfer tax that is due

The office records original, signed, notarized papers. The one kind of copy it will accept is a certified copy of a document already recorded with another government office. If the deed needs an oath of consideration, the oath must be notarized too. A missing parcel number or a deed with no preparer name is a common reason for a rejected recording, so have the title company or attorney run through the list before closing day.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a Davidson County sale?
sections.html:
Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 for each $100 of the purchase price, and the Department of Revenue says the buyer, as grantee, pays it to the register. The mortgage tax is a separate charge of $0.115 per $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 exempt, and the borrower pays it.

The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate puts the median owner-occupied home in Davidson County at $417,400. At that figure the transfer tax would be about $1,544.38. A real sale is taxed on its own price or market value, so the number on your contract is the one that counts.

The Department of Revenue states that no oath of value is needed when a transfer is exempt. Transfers that end a tenancy by the entirety or divide property held by tenants in common are among the exempt ones listed in the county training materials, along with leasehold estates.

sections.h2: What is Davidson County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Davidson County was created in 1783 and named for General William Lee Davidson of North Carolina. It covers 526 square miles, of which 504 are land, and the Cumberland River runs east to west through the middle. The Metropolitan Nashville Public Schools district serves the whole county, and several small cities that incorporated before consolidation kept some independence.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts show a market that is larger and more rental-heavy than the rest of the state:

  • 745,904 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up from 715,887 in the April 2020 base
  • Owner-occupied housing rate of 52.8 percent, so nearly half of households rent
  • Median gross rent of $1,582 a month and median household income of $77,853
  • 5,632 building permits in 2025 and 389,379 housing units

About 15 percent of residents were born outside the United States, and 48.4 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. A seller with a dated or inherited house here has a large pool of renters and newcomers to consider, and a cash sale is one route to weigh against a listing.

sections.h2: How does recording connect to property tax when you sell in Davidson County?
sections.html:
Recording moves ownership on the public record. It does not pay the tax bill. County property tax is billed from the assessment as of January 1, and the Tennessee Comptroller's schedule sets taxes as due on the first Monday of October and delinquent after the last day of February.

Ask the Metropolitan Trustee, whose office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., what is owed on your parcel before you close. Your closing agent will normally request the figure too. If you think the appraisal is too high, the Comptroller says an appeal starts with the county board of equalization and can then go to the State Board of Equalization, which must receive it by August 1 or within 45 days of the local board's notice, whichever is later.

A seller who is 65 or older or disabled may qualify for the state's tax relief program, which pays part of a homeowner's tax on up to $33,600 of market value when income is no more than $38,470. Applications go to the trustee.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Davidson County?
faqs.a: The Davidson County Register of Deeds, at 300 Deaderick Street in Nashville. The office is part of Metro government and is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., phone 615-862-6790. It holds deeds, deeds of trust, releases, liens and plats.

faqs.q: Can I record a copy of my deed instead of the original?
faqs.a: No, except for one case. The office accepts only original, signed, notarized documents, apart from a certified copy of something already recorded in another government office.

faqs.q: How much does the register charge for a copy of a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Uncertified copies are $0.50 a page and certified copies are $1 a page. A mailed request has a $2 minimum, and a mailed subdivision plat costs $5.

faqs.q: Does the Davidson County register tell me whether my house has liens?
faqs.a: No. The staff say a lien check needs a title search by an attorney or title company. The indexes are open to the public on office computers, and the register does not draft deeds either.

faqs.q: Is there a way to be warned about a fraudulent deed filed against my house?
faqs.a: Yes. Property Alert is a free service from the register that sends an email if any document is filed under your name. You can sign up through the office website or the mobile app.
